en: Paṭṭhānapakaraṇa:
Dhammānulomapaccanīya (3), Tikadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (4) 16.4.
Kusala-ttika, Hetu-sahetuka-duka.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots, an unwholesome state that is neither a root nor accompanied by roots arises by way of the root condition.

Dependent on a wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots, an indeterminate state that is neither a root nor accompanied by roots arises by way of the root condition. [Dependent on] a wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots...

Dependent on a state that is unwholesome, not a root, and neither-root-nor-non-root, as well as a state that is indeterminate, not a root, and neither-root-nor-non-root, states that are unwholesome, not roots, and neither-root-nor-non-root arise by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is unwholesome, both a root and accompanied by a root, a state that is not wholesome, not a root, and neither-root-nor-non-root arises by way of root-condition. … [Three.]
Dependent on an indeterminate state that is both a root and accompanied by roots, there arises a state that is neither wholesome nor a root and is not without roots, by way of root-condition.

Dependent on an indeterminate state that is both a root and accompanied by roots, there arises a state that is neither unwholesome nor a root and is not without roots, by way of root-condition. [Dependent on] an indeterminate state that is both a root and accompanied by roots...

And a state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on an unwholesome state that is both accompanied by roots and not itself a root, there arises a state that is neither indeterminate nor without roots and is also neither non-root nor accompanied by roots, by way of root condition.
